advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or replace test_the_hand_copied_literal_is_gone: it greps the source-under-test AST/text instead of asserting behavior already covered by the derived-set equality test.
evidence: assert literal_sets == [], "the layer labels are re-listed as a literal collection"
assert "_SOURCE_KINDS" not in source, "the hand-copied constant is still present"
The unit under test is Python source (src/rebar/_operation_config.py), not an instruction artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-grep exception does not apply.
Refactoring-violation criterion: renaming the private constant or re-listing the labels as documentation preserves behavior yet fails this test.
advisory.finding: test_the_hand_copied_literal_is_gone asserts against the SOURCE TEXT/AST of the unit under test (absence of the literal collection and of the name '_SOURCE_KINDS') rather than observable behavior. This is a source-grepping / change-detector test: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (re-introducing the labels as a doc example, or a differently-named private constant) with no change to what the code does, and it adds no regression-catching power beyond test_derived_set_equals_layer_order.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove test_source_kinds_imports_rebar_config_inside_its_own_body: the deferral behavior is already verified by the cold-import subprocess test; the AST-location assertion is a change-detector.
evidence: deferred = {node.module for node in ast.walk(func) if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module}
Refactoring-violation criterion (Rule 4): a differently-structured but still-deferred import passes the behavioral subprocess test yet fails this AST-shape assertion.
advisory.finding: test_source_kinds_imports_rebar_config_inside_its_own_body asserts on the AST location of the import statement (import must live inside the _source_kinds function body). This is a change-detector on implementation structure: any behavior-preserving way to avoid the import cycle (e.g. a module-scope TYPE_CHECKING guard plus a lazy accessor, or extracting the import into a helper) would fail it despite identical observable behavior. The real deferral guarantee is already covered behaviorally by test_derivation_does_not_run_until_the_accessor_is_called (a cold subprocess import).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider removing test_rebar_config_is_not_imported_at_module_scope: it asserts import AST shape, duplicating the behavioral cold-import guarantee without added regression power.
evidence: assert not any(target == "rebar.config" or target.startswith("rebar.config.") for target in _module_scope_import_targets())

The observable failure mode (import cycle on cold import) is already exercised by test_derivation_does_not_run_until_the_accessor_is_called, which imports rebar._operation_config in a fresh interpreter.
advisory.finding: test_rebar_config_is_not_imported_at_module_scope asserts on module-scope import AST rather than the observable outcome (a cold `import rebar.config` succeeds). It is a change-detector: it fails only on a structural change and provides no regression signal that the behavioral cold-import test does not already provide.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace test_every_use_site_treats_the_vocabulary_as_a_membership_set with a behavioral assertion; the AST Compare-node check breaks on equivalent membership rewrites.
evidence: assert id(call) in membership_operands, ("a use site consumes the vocabulary as something other than a membership test; ...")
Refactoring-violation criterion: a `.issuperset(...)`/local-variable rewrite is a membership use that still fails this Compare-node assertion.
advisory.finding: test_every_use_site_treats_the_vocabulary_as_a_membership_set asserts that every _source_kinds() call node is an operand of an `in`/`not in` Compare in the AST. This couples the test to the syntactic form of the call sites; a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. `if not _source_kinds().issuperset({label})`, or assigning the frozenset to a local before the membership check) breaks it without any change to observable behavior. AC3's real guarantee (order is not consumed) is behaviorally covered by the label-acceptance/rejection tests.
